When starting an action that is not configured a streaming, we still appear to ask the agent to prepare a plan.

codex replied with:

> Iâ€™ll use update_plan for multi-step work and explicit task lists, and skip it for simple requests and answer-only questions.

No plan request was done, it was just to shorten a text.

so most likely, we also pass the switch to use plans when we are in non-streaming mode. this is wrong.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

title: agent task list component
status: ready

Part of [F_380](F_380_add_possibility_to_support_task_tracking_tool.md). Show `conversation.taskList` from [F_431](F_431_agent_task_list_model_and_run_update.md) in the conversation chat.

## Current state

* `ActionConversationChat` (`app/src/components/actions/conversation/action_conversation_chat.tsx`) lays out the transcript, status area and prompt.
* Live conversations come from the run store in `action_run_registry.ts`; historical ones from `ActionConversationStore` (`resolveDisplayedConversation`).

## Implementation details

* New self-contained component `AgentTaskList` in `app/src/components/actions/conversation/tasks/agent_task_list.tsx`. It receives only what identifies the displayed conversation and subscribes itself with `useSyncExternalStore`; `getSnapshot` returns `conversation.taskList` (a stable reference that changes only on `agentTaskList`). No task data or handlers come from the parent, so it can be moved elsewhere later.
* Initial placement: in `ActionConversationChat`, directly above the prompt.
* Renders nothing when there is no list or it is empty.
* Each row: status icon (pending / in progress / completed) and text; an in-progress task shows `activeForm` when present, otherwise `subject`. Header shows `completed/total`. Collapsible, expanded by default, compact height with scrolling for long lists.
* Styling per `design/STYLE_GUIDE.md` and the existing conversation status components.
* Works the same for live and historical conversations.

## Tests

React Testing Library:

* Renders tasks with their states and the progress count.
* Shows `activeForm` for the in-progress task.
* Renders nothing without a task list.
* Updates when an `agentTaskList` update arrives.

We recently implemented support for task lists. this is working ok for claude, but not for codex. Investigate why this is.

## Findings

* Task tracking is enabled in the desktop configuration. The task-list model, persistence and UI are working.
* Both Codex paths already decode task updates: streaming handles `turn/plan/updated`; one-shot handles `todo_list` lifecycle items.
* Claude is explicitly given its task tools when tracking is enabled. Codex is not explicitly enabled: MDÂ² only adds `tools.update_plan.enabled=false` when tracking is disabled and otherwise relies on the Codex default.
* MDÂ² does not instruct Codex to use `update_plan`. Having the tool available does not require the model to call it, even when an action prompt asks it to create tasks.
* Codex app-server supports `developerInstructions` on both `thread/start` and `thread/resume`. This is the appropriate boundary for a persistent Codex-only task-tracking instruction.
* Codex Goals are not a replacement for this task list. A Goal is one persistent objective; the existing component represents multiple plan steps.

## Implementation plan

1. Change Codex command construction to always set `tools.update_plan.enabled` explicitly: `true` when agent task tracking is enabled and `false` when disabled. Keep Claude command behavior unchanged.
2. When tracking is enabled, pass a concise Codex `developerInstructions` value on new and resumed streaming threads. Require Codex to use and maintain `update_plan` for multi-step work and whenever the user explicitly requests tasks. Do not create a plan for a simple one-step request or answer-only question.
3. Apply the equivalent instruction at the prompt boundary for one-shot Codex runs, which do not use app-server thread settings.
4. Keep the existing task-list decoders, persistence and React component unchanged.
5. Add targeted tests for enabled and disabled Codex commands, new and resumed thread instructions, one-shot prompt instructions, and plan/todo updates reaching the existing task-list update path.

Part of [F_380](F_380_add_possibility_to_support_task_tracking_tool.md). Turn Claude's task tool calls into the task list from [F_431](F_431_agent_task_list_model_and_run_update.md). Needs [F_430](F_430_agent_task_tracking_setting.md) for Claude to have the tools.

## Current state

* Claude task tools arrive as ordinary `tool_use` blocks. Streaming renders them through `claudeToolEvent` (`agent_claude_streaming_adapter.js`) as `tool.TaskCreate` / `tool.TaskUpdate` rows with raw JSON; one-shot records them through `claudeTranscriptEvents` (`agent_claude_events.js`).
* `agent_claude_events.js` holds decoders shared by the one-shot parser (`agent_provider_protocol.js`) and `ClaudeStreamingAdapter`; new decoders must live there. `ClaudeFileResultDecoder` already pairs a `tool_use` with its `tool_result` and reads `tool_use_result` when one result block is present.
* Sub-agent events carry `parent_tool_use_id`.

## Implementation details

* Add `ClaudeTaskListDecoder` (own file) used by both paths:
  * `TaskCreate`: remember `{ subject, activeForm }` by `tool_use.id`. On the matching `tool_result`, read the task id from `tool_use_result.task.id` and add the task as `pending`. Ignore results with `is_error`.
  * `TaskUpdate`: read the id from `taskId`, falling back to `id` / `task_id` (Claude Code repairs these names before execution, the stream shows the raw input). Apply `status` (`in_progress` â†’ `inProgress`), `subject`, `activeForm`. `status: 'deleted'` removes the task. Unknown ids are logged and skipped.
  * Each change emits the full list as a `taskList` run event.
  * `TodoWrite` is not decoded (only appears with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0`, which md2 does not set).
* Sub agents: merge their task changes into the same list. Task ids are expected to be unique per Claude session; verify during implementation. If ids collide between parent and sub agent, key sub-agent tasks by `parent_tool_use_id` + task id.
* Hide: task tool calls and their results produce no transcript entries in either path. `TaskGet` and `TaskList` are hidden too; they read state and change nothing.
* Reset decoder state where `ClaudeFileResultDecoder.reset()` is called.

## Edge cases

* After `--resume`, Claude's own task state may differ from the stored list; the stored list shows until the next change replaces it.
* A `TaskUpdate` before its `TaskCreate` result arrives: skipped and logged.

## Tests

Fixture stream-json events, run through both the one-shot parser and `ClaudeStreamingAdapter`:

* create â†’ update â†’ complete â†’ delete produces the expected lists.
* Fallback id keys, `is_error` results, sub-agent tasks merged.
* No transcript entries for task tools.

Findings:

- The suspicion is correct. `resolveAgentExecution` enables task tracking for both streaming and non-streaming runs.
- For one-shot Codex runs, `AgentRunnerService` also prepends the task-tracking instruction directly to the user prompt. The quoted response closely paraphrases that injected text.
- Claude task tools are likewise enabled for one-shot runs.
- One-shot parsing and UI technically support task lists, so this is an intentional behavior from B_319, not a missing capability.

Proposed solution:

- Enable task tracking only when `streaming && agentTaskTrackingEnabled`.
- Remove the one-shot Codex prompt injection.
- Explicitly disable Codex’s `update_plan` tool and Claude’s task tools for non-streaming runs.
- Update focused execution, environment, and runner tests for both providers.

When starting an action that is not configured a streaming, we still appear to ask the agent to prepare a plan.

codex replied with:

No plan request was done, it was just to shorten a text.

so most likely, we also pass the switch to use plans when we are in non-streaming mode. this is wrong.

## Current state

* `resolveAgentExecution` applies `desktop.agentTaskTrackingEnabled` to both streaming and non-streaming runs.
* Non-streaming Codex commands explicitly enable `tools.update_plan` when task tracking is enabled. `AgentRunnerService` also prepends the Codex task-tracking instruction to the one-shot user prompt. This injected text can be treated as part of a simple transformation request, which explains the observed response.
* Non-streaming Claude runs likewise receive the environment setting that enables task tools.
* The one-shot provider parser and conversation UI can decode and display task lists, but non-streaming actions must not request or use them.

## Implementation details

* In `resolveAgentExecution`, derive the effective task-tracking value as `streaming && config.agentTaskTrackingEnabled`. Use that value for command construction and return it in the resolved execution settings so downstream Codex and Claude paths receive the same decision.
* Remove `codexOneShotPrompt` and stop modifying non-streaming Codex prompts. Keep the shared Codex task-tracking instruction for streaming app-server sessions.
* Keep the existing task-list decoders, persistence, and conversation UI unchanged. Historical task lists and streaming task tracking remain supported.
* Update the task-tracking configuration description to state that it applies to streaming conversations.
* Add focused tests proving that non-streaming Codex disables `update_plan`, non-streaming Claude does not enable task tools, and one-shot prompts remain unchanged. Retain coverage for enabled streaming runs.

## Acceptance criteria

* Starting a non-streaming action never enables Codex `update_plan` or Claude task tools, regardless of the desktop task-tracking setting.
* A non-streaming Codex action receives the original action prompt without task-tracking instructions.
* Simple non-streaming transformations do not produce responses that repeat or paraphrase hidden task-tracking instructions.
* Streaming Codex and Claude conversations still receive task-tracking instructions and tools when task tracking is enabled.
* Disabling task tracking continues to disable task tools in both execution modes.
* Existing task-list decoding, persistence, and rendering behavior remains unchanged.
